system_config.scenario_scale: Toy projects and undergraduate-level applications (Exclude everything listed in inputs.out_of_scope and enterprise over-engineering)
system_config.technical_depth: Advanced CS undergraduate level (Focus on the internal mechanisms listed in inputs.focus_mechanisms)

task: Review inputs.outline.deep_dive_sections. Remove sections that are weakly related or duplicated. If fewer than 3 sections remain, write new sections to bring the count back to 3. Return the full outline in the same structure.
review_criteria: out_of_scope: Remove a section whose explanation depends on anything listed in inputs.out_of_scope.

weak_relevance: Remove a section if deleting it would leave the cause of the problem in outline.introduction.problem_statement explained just as well, i.e., its mechanism_explanation does not lead to the observed wrong result.

duplication: If two sections rely on the same principle, keep the one with the clearer causal chain and remove the other. Judge by principle, not by wording: two sections that end in a similar observed result but rest on different principles are not duplicates.
constraints: output_language: Write every string value in English, except core_message, which stays exactly as given.
remove_only_by_criteria: Remove a section only when it meets one of review_criteria. Never remove a section just to shorten the outline.
preserve_verbatim: Copy every kept section and every field outside deep_dive_sections exactly as given. Do NOT rewrite, polish, merge, or reorder them.
refill_only_when_short: Add new sections only if fewer than 3 sections remain after removal, and add exactly as many as needed to reach 3. If 3 or more remain, add nothing.

refill_source: Each new section must cover an item of inputs.focus_mechanisms that no section in inputs.outline (kept or removed) covered. If none is left, use a closely related mechanism that explains the problem in problem_statement. A new section must not meet any review_criteria itself.
refill_position: Insert each new section where it fits the logical flow among the kept sections.
argument_placement: A new section explains why the problem in problem_statement occurs. Do NOT state the core_argument's solution in it.

principle_shape: Write principle of every new section as exactly two sentences: (1) a topic sentence stating how the mechanism works, which the paragraph will develop, and (2) a concluding sentence stating what necessarily follows from it, independent of the scenario. Name a framework class or method only if the reader will meet it in logs, stack traces, or while debugging.

causal_mechanism: Write mechanism_explanation of every new section as one declarative causal sentence following the structure: 'When [A: the code path from the problem situation] executes, due to [B: the principle], [C: the observed result] occurs.'
no_instruction_terms: Never write the project scale, audience level, or wording from these instructions (e.g., 'toy project', 'undergraduate', 'dilemma') into output text.
no_meta_commentary: Strictly forbid meta-statements explaining the purpose of the article (e.g., 'This article explores...', 'Let's take a look at...').
concise_takeaway: Compress key_takeaway of every new section into a single English noun phrase of at most 10 words.

outline.description: Revised outline with exactly the same keys and structure as inputs.outline; deep_dive_sections has at least 3 items

review_log.description: One entry per removed or added section; empty array if nothing changed

reason.description: One English sentence. For removed: which review_criteria applied and why. For added: which gap it fills.
